review_type: single AI curator; full received final answer read; model identity visible

errors.quote: net synthesis is only measurable if the buffer sits below ATP-synthesis equilibrium
errors.issue: Incorrect: the purpose of mechanical work is to enable synthesis against a positive chemical free-energy requirement. Below-equilibrium formation can occur without work and cannot by itself establish chemical-energy storage. Reaction activities and mechanical work must jointly determine the interpretation.

errors.quote: no PK/PEP that would consume ATP or confound
errors.issue: Pyruvate kinase plus phosphoenolpyruvate regenerates ATP from ADP; it does not consume ATP in the stated regeneration system. Excluding it is appropriate, but the biochemical explanation is reversed.

Even within a calibrated linear range, this is ATP concentration under a consuming reporter, not net synthesis flux. The protocol lacks reporter-consumption/response-time modeling or a reporter-free product-inventory arm needed for its turn-proportional synthesis estimate.

There is no corresponding phosphate-omission test, and no measured initial bound ATP inventory or repeated-turnover bound. ADP dependence and an AK inhibitor do not alone establish new ATP from ADP plus phosphate.

errors.quote: report coupling efficiency as (measured slope)/(3 ATP per turn)
errors.issue: This is a stoichiometric yield relative to an assumed ideal, not energetic efficiency. Energy conversion additionally needs transmitted torque/work and the actual chemical free-energy change.

errors.quote: By near-universal convention this is **counterclockwise (CCW)** viewed from the F1 side
errors.issue: The surrounding paragraph mixes membrane/anchoring and opposite F1-side viewpoints. Assign the sign from observed hydrolysis in the actual optical geometry and characterize surface orientations, rather than relying on the inconsistent universal convention.

errors.quote: C is positively identified only when rotation is verified
errors.issue: Verified motion plus a null readout does not positively identify a one-way rectifier without adequate sensitivity, coverage, retained activity and operating-range checks. Later conditional caveats narrow the claim but do not repair this categorical table/decision rule.

rationale: Recognizes the correct question and includes simultaneous tracking, reporter controls and explicit single-molecule attribution limits. The thermodynamic requirement is reversed, consuming-reporter output is not converted into synthesis flux, and stoichiometric yield is called efficiency. Substrate and initial-pool controls are incomplete. These errors materially weaken the main energy-conversion inference.
reference_guardrails: The packet establishes ATP-associated directional motion, not an ATP-per-turn yield, torque, universal camera sign or completed reverse-synthesis experiment. Proposed numerical settings may earn credit when explicitly qualified.
Correct the draft reference by explicitly requiring magnesium/cofactor and nucleotide speciation qualification; its generic reaction inventory is not a complete buffer recipe.
Reverse operation should generate new ATP repeatedly beyond measured initial available/bound pools. Three catalytic sites are not a universal total ATP-contamination bound.

Luciferase is an acceptable chemical readout when its consumption, recovery and time response are calibrated. An intensity slope is not generally synthesis flux; chromatographic detection is an alternative, not mandatory.
Label incorporation can reflect exchange. Pair isotope provenance with net-product/material balance; account for reporter consumption and sample removal as appropriate.
Empirical direction, mixed surface orientations, actual rotor turns and transmitted torque are distinct quantities. Do not replace any with the nominal actuator command.

Mechanical input can drive ATP synthesis uphill. Low initial ATP may aid sensitivity but does not prove positive chemical-energy storage; energetic efficiency needs both work and chemical free energy.

ATP per turn is a coupling yield, not energetic efficiency. Inactive fractions, orientation, incomplete entrainment and analytical recovery can reduce apparent yield without establishing loose molecular coupling.
Separate ADP and phosphate controls help discriminate intended synthesis from alternative ATP production. Inhibitor effects require assay and enzyme specificity validation.

Matching is retrospective and applies all five predeclared components. A partially correct historical direction is recorded even when the experimental design is flawed; no claim of prospective novelty or uncontaminated holdout is made.
